subject: axolotl

Category: Animal.
Subject: axolotl with frilly pink gills.
Style: chibi.

spec.name: Pip the Chibi Axolotl
spec.description: A chibi axolotl with a huge round head, frilly coral-pink external gills, a wide contented smile and a broad ribbon tail, standing on four stubby legs.
spec.layout: A chibi salamander facing +Z, roughly one-third head, one-third body, one-third tail. The head is an oversized rounded dome (the hero feature) whose sides carry three pairs of coral gill stalks fanning up, out and back, each stalk dressed with soft frilly filaments; the face is wide and flat with two small dark bead eyes set far apart, tiny nostrils, rosy cheek blushes and a very wide gentle smile with a thin darker mouth line. The torso is a short plump capsule lower than the head, with a cream belly and a faint dorsal ridge. Four very short stubby legs (front pair at the chest, hind pair under the hips) end in little rounded feet with three toes each, and they are the only parts touching the floor. The tail is a thick root that tapers into a broad flat fin ribbon sweeping back to z = -0.62, with a slightly transparent-look lighter fin edge. The style is bold and toy-like: every shape a chunky primitive, gills and smile oversized, cheeks blushing, belly pale, all flat colours with the coral gills as the loudest accent against the soft pink skin.

parts.builds: The oversized chibi head and every face feature plus the gill crowns. Skull: a large rounded dome (sphere or lofted capsule roughly 0.34 m wide and 0.3 m tall) in skin pink, slightly wider than tall, with a short blunt snout box/loft protruding to z = 0.4 in skin pink with a cream chin and underside. Face (all on the head bone, nothing in front of the eyes): two small glossy bead eyes (dark ink spheres with a white shine stud each) set wide at about x = ±0.1, y = 0.26; tiny ink nostril dots on the snout tip; a very wide smile built as a shallow swept ink mouth line across the front from x = -0.11 to x = 0.11 with small upturned corner ticks; rosy blush ovals (flat pink discs) under each eye. The signature feature: three gill stalks per side rising from the head's upper sides on the gillLT/gillLM/gillLB joints, each stalk a short tapering sweep in gill coral that fans outward and back, and each stalk carrying 5-7 soft frilly filaments (small tapered spikes or short swept fronds alternating gill coral and gill light) branching off both sides along its length, the fronds longest on the top stalk so the crown reads instantly. Give each gill joint a small rest-pose splay so the frills are separated and readable.
parts.attaches: The skull's lower back sits over the neck mount [0, 0.22, 0.12], overlapping the body part's front; its underside meets the jaw mount. All geometry rides the head, jaw and gill joints.

parts.builds: The plump torso between head and tail. A short horizontal capsule or loft (about 0.24 m wide, 0.14 m tall, from z = -0.26 to z = 0.14) in skin pink, sagging slightly lower at the belly. Belly: a cream underside built as either a paint-free second loft or stuck belly plates covering the lower third. A subtle dorsal ridge: a row of 6-8 tiny rounded skin-shadow studs or a low frill running along the spine from the neck mount back to the tailRoot mount. Small shoulder and hip smooth bulges where the legs attach, and a soft neck crease ring where the head overlaps. The body's top surface is a touch warmer pink, its underside cream, keeping the countershade reading.
parts.attaches: Front face meets the head part at the neck mount [0, 0.22, 0.12]; rear face meets the tail part at the tailRoot mount [0, 0.16, -0.22]; undersides open at the four leg-socket mounts (shoulderFL/FR, hipHL/HR). Rides the body joint.

parts.builds: Four stubby chibi legs with feet and toes. Each leg: a short thick tapered tube or two-sweep limb from its socket mount down to the floor, in skin pink with a skin-shadow crease ring at the ankle, ending in a rounded foot (a squashed sphere or low dome in toe pink) whose bottom rests exactly on y = 0. Each foot carries three small toe bumps (tiny spheres or short digit spikes) fanning forward, in toe pink, plus a small pale claw nub per toe. Front pair slightly shorter and turned a few degrees outward, hind pair a touch sturdier. All four legs identical in construction, mirrored across x = 0.
parts.attaches: Each leg's top socket meets the body part at its named mount (shoulderFL, shoulderFR, hipHL, hipHR) and is hidden inside the torso's lower edge. Rides that leg's leg and foot joints.

parts.builds: The broad ribbon tail with its fin. Tail root: a thick tapering sweep continuing the body line from the tailRoot mount back to about z = -0.5, in skin pink with a cream underside. Fin: a wide flat membrane or extruded fin lobe wrapping the tail's last third, from the dorsal ridge line down past the belly line on both sides (top fin and bottom fin lobes or one full caudal fin), in finEdge pink, lighter and thinner toward the scalloped trailing edge so it reads as translucent against the body; the fin's root joins smoothly into the tail root's skin. Give the fin a soft wavy or scalloped trailing edge and a faint midline seam in skin shadow where fin meets tail. Tip of the tail rounds off at z = -0.62.
parts.attaches: Front face meets the body part at the tailRoot mount [0, 0.16, -0.22], its root radius matching the torso's rear. Rides the tail1, tail2 and tail3 joints.

calls.reasoning:
I need to write a spec JSON for a chibi axolotl with frilly pink gills. Three to six parts, joints, palette, mounts, boxes, budgets.

Axolotl chibi: big head, small body, four stubby legs, broad tail fin, external feathery gills (3 pairs branching from head sides), wide smiling mouth, small eyes, pale pink/purple palette.

Layout: faces +Z (front). Axolotl length maybe 0.5m real... chibi axolotl, keep real-world-ish small salamander ~0.3 m, but chibi proportions. Let's set size ~ [0.55, 0.35, 0.75] m.

Parts: head (with gills, face), body/torso, legs (4), tail. Maybe combine gills into head part. 4 parts:
- head with gills and face: box x -0.25..0.25, y 0.05..0.33, z 0.05..0.38
- body: torso
- legs: 4 stubby legs
- tail: long tail with dorsal fin

Mounts: neck joint where head meets body.

Joints: root spine at body; head joint; 4 leg joints; tail chain; maybe gill joints (3 per side, role fan/hinge?). Gills could be a ring with joints for animation. Let's define:

- root "spine" at [0, 0.14, -0.02], dir [0,1,0]? Actually axolotl body horizontal. Root joint maybe "hips" at [0,0.16,-0.1], role spine.
- head at [0, 0.2, 0.14], dir [0,0.3,1] role head.
- jaw at head, role jaw.
- gill joints: gillLA1..3 and gillRA1..3 as hinge/fan? Could use group. Keep simpler: three per side as joints with role "fan"? Roles allowed: spine neck head jaw hinge tail leg arm wing digit tentacle fan. Gill stalks → "fan" role, group "gills".
- tail chain: tail1..3 role tail.
- legs: legFL etc role leg, each single joint? Better chains with hip/knee... keep simple: one joint per leg, role leg, group legs. Or two joints per leg (hip, ankle). Budget-wise fine; spec can say chain of 2 per leg.

Let me define joints explicitly in order, parents first:

1. body (root) at [0, 0.16, -0.05], dir [0, 1, 0], role spine
2. head, parent body, at [0, 0.22, 0.12], dir [0, 0.35, 1], role head
3. jaw, parent head, at [0, 0.15, 0.2], dir [0, -0.5, 1], role jaw
4. gillL1, parent head, at [0.16, 0.28, 0.12], dir [1, 0.3, 0.6], role fan, group gills
5. gillL2, parent head, at [0.17, 0.24, 0.08], dir [1, 0, 0.8], role fan, group gills
6. gillL3, parent head, at [0.16, 0.2, 0.04], dir [1, -0.3, 0.7], role fan, group gills
7-9. gillR1..3 mirrored.
10. tail1, parent body, at [0, 0.16, -0.22], dir [0, 0, -1], role tail
11. tail2, parent tail1, at [0, 0.17, -0.4], dir [0, 0, -1], role tail
12. tail3, parent tail2, at [0, 0.18, -0.55], dir [0, 0.1, -1], role tail
13-16. legs: legFL, parent body, at [0.09, 0.1, 0.02], dir [0,-1,0.2], role leg; legFR, legHL at z -0.16, legHR.

Maybe each leg one joint is fine for rigging? System says limbs chains with hip/knee preferred, but spec can have 2 per leg. To keep joint count reasonable but rig-friendly, do hip+ankle? I'll do single leg joints with role leg — acceptable ("a hand, foot or hoof is the tip of its arm or leg chain" — chain of one). Actually better give each leg two joints: e.g. legFL (hip, dir down-forward) and footFL tip. Keep one per leg for simplicity; the builders build stubby legs. Hmm, rig answer key: leg chain contact. Single-joint leg chain works.

Actually let's give each leg 2 joints: hip and ankle (tip). Names legFL/ankleFL. That's 8 leg joints. Total joints: 1+2+6+3+8 = 20. Fine.

Tail: 3 joints. Total 20.

Mounts: neck mount [0, 0.22, 0.12] where head meets body; tailRoot [0, 0.16, -0.22]; leg sockets (hip points). Mounts keys: neck, tailRoot, shoulderFL, shoulderFR, hipHL, hipHR, floor?

Parts (4):
1. head: skull, snout/mouth, eyes, gill stalks with frilly filaments. box [[-0.26, 0.08, 0.06], [0.26, 0.34, 0.40]]. attaches at neck mount, jaw + gill joints. budget ~150.
2. body: torso, belly, back ridge, tiny arms? No—legs separate part. body box [[-0.14, 0.08, -0.28], [0.14, 0.24, 0.16]]. budget ~80. Includes smile? no face is head. Includes back dorsal ridge? Axolotl doesn't have much. Add dorsal crest ridge and belly.
3. legs: 4 stubby legs with toes. box [[-0.2, 0.0, -0.24], [0.2, 0.12, 0.1]]. floor true. budget ~100.
4. tail: tail + fin membrane. box [[-0.16, 0.05, -0.62], [0.16, 0.26, -0.2]]. budget ~90.

Budgets sum ≤900: 150+80+100+90=420 fine; but budgets should reflect richness; can raise. 160+90+120+110=480.

Palette (≤24):
- skinPink main "#f2a7c3" (axolotl pink)
- bellyCream "#fde8ee" or "#fff0f5"
- gillCoral "#ff5c8a" deep pink for gills
- gillLight "#ff9ebc"
- ink "#3a2438" dark plum for eyes/mouth line
- eyeWhite "#ffffff"
- irisDark "#2a1832"
- blush "#ff8fb0"
- toePink "#e989ad"
- nostrilDark? use ink.

That's ~9 colours. Good.

Size: width including gills ~0.55 (gills stick out), height ~0.35, length 0.75. Gills stick to sides: head box to ±0.26. Tail length to -0.62. So size [0.55, 0.36, 0.8]. Fine for a chibi axolotl (stylized, larger than real but plausible pet-size; chibi style justifies chunky). Real axolotl ~23cm; chibi head-heavy 0.5m is fine-ish. Keep it.
